transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling incredibly depressed, sad, and empty inside for a really long time now. It has been going on constantly for about two years and four months, and I just can't seem to shake this heavy mood.
During these two years, have you experienced any periods where your mood significantly shifted, such as feeling extremely happy, irritable, or energetic, even if it was just for a short time?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. My mood has just been consistently low, sad, and empty this entire time. I've never had any periods of high energy or extreme happiness.
Can you tell me if there have been any periods over the past two years where your depressive symptoms have worsened or improved, even slightly, or have they remained relatively constant?

They have remained pretty much constant. I haven't had any periods of improvement or times where I felt back to normal over these past two years and four months. It has just been a steady, unchanging sadness every single day.
How have you been able to manage your daily activities, such as work, social interactions, and personal care, despite feeling this constant sadness?

Managing daily activities has been extremely difficult, and honestly, I'm not really sure how I've been getting by lately. Even making minor daily choices or trying to focus on simple tasks feels completely overwhelming. I just feel like I'm dragging myself through each day.

Have you experienced at least two of the following symptoms nearly every day for the past two weeks: significant weight loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue or loss of energy, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, diminished ability to think or concentrate, or recurrent thoughts of death?

Yes, I've struggled with sleep issues and concentration difficulties for over two years, not just two weeks. My sleep is completely broken—I either can't fall asleep, wake up constantly, or sleep way too much—and my mind feels so foggy that I can't focus or make simple decisions. However, I haven't experienced things like weight changes, guilt, or thoughts of death.
Can you tell me more about when your sleep issues and concentration difficulties started, and have they been present for the majority of the past two years, or have they come and gone?

Both my sleep problems and my trouble concentrating started about two years and four months ago, right when this low mood began. They haven't really come and gone at all; they've been persistently present for the majority of this entire time.

Have you had a period of at least two weeks during the past two years where your depressive symptoms met the full criteria for a major depressive episode, with at least five of the typical symptoms being present, or has your depression been more chronic and lower-grade?

My depression has been more of a chronic, lower-grade struggle that has just been constantly there. I haven't had any distinct two-week periods where it suddenly became much more severe; it has just been a steady, continuous weight for the past two years and four months.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms have remained relatively constant over the past two years and four months, with no distinct periods of significant improvement or worsening, and no episodes of major depressive episodes lasting at least two weeks. This pattern, along with the presence of chronic low mood, sleep disturbances, and concentration difficulties, aligns more closely with Persistent Depressive Disorder than Major Depressive Disorder, which typically involves one or more discrete major depressive episodes. The lack of periods with elevated mood, high energy, or extreme happiness also reduces the likelihood of other mood disorders. Therefore, Persistent Depressive Disorder is the most fitting diagnosis based on the provided information.
